back: Fuel, heat and oxygen: the three requirements for a fire. Removing one puts out the fire.
Mediterranean-climate regions (California, Mediterranean basin, south-west Australia, Chile, the Western Cape), boreal forests, savannas and cleared tropical forests and peatlands.
Physical: lightning, sparks from falling rocks. Human: accidents (cigarettes, campfires, power lines, escaped burning) and arson or land-clearing fires.
Fuel (dry and continuous), wind (and spotting by embers), topography (faster uphill), and weather (hot, dry air).
The zone where buildings meet or mix with natural vegetation: the area of greatest risk to people and property.
Danger ratings and satellite monitoring, prescribed burning and firebreaks, defensible space, planning, education and law, firefighting and evacuation, recovery.
Victoria, Australia: extreme heat and wind; 173 deaths and about 2 000 homes destroyed.
California: 85 deaths and about 18 000 buildings destroyed; investigators linked the ignition to electrical equipment.
Longer, hotter, drier fire seasons and more extreme fire weather raise the risk and severity; a fire still needs an ignition source.
